content.text: {"core": "Abstraction lifts a thing into an idea about the thing — the pattern behind the mess, the rule under the cases. In its own position, that lifting turns on itself: the pattern-making becomes the very thing patterned. Starved, the lifting never rises — everything stays a pile of separate cases, and no idea ever forms that would let one instance teach the next.", "sheetLine": "Each thing stays its own thing; nothing rises into a pattern that carries over."}
